search_log: Searched “Michael Crichton Dragon Teeth excerpt chapter narration,” “Dragon Teeth Michael Crichton point of view third person narrator,” “site:michaelcrichton.com Dragon Teeth excerpt,” and “site:harpercollins.com Dragon Teeth Michael Crichton excerpt.”

Opened and assessed the Penguin Random House Spanish publisher excerpt, BookRags point-of-view analysis, Bookreporter English excerpt, Kirkus audiobook review, and Google Books record; the Kirkus and Google Books pages described Johnson’s perspective or plot but did not explicitly establish grammatical narrative person.

Searched exact passages “Religion explains what man cannot explain” and “I am most heartily glad that I am not going to the dangerous and uncertain Black Hills”; fuller contexts showed the former is Cope’s speech and the latter is a quoted Johnson journal note.

Searched “Dragon Teeth omniscient third-person narrator” and “Dragon Teeth third-person William Johnson”; found explicit whole-book descriptions from BookRags and Deep Time Dispatches, with the latter specifically distinguishing the third-person narrative from occasional journal excerpts.
No credible source found evidence of sustained second-person narration or autonomous first-person base sections; inaccessible previews and plot-summary grammar were not used as person evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrative is third person, principally focalized through William Johnson. Goodreads supplies sustained third-person framing in q02171 and q02174, while the authorized publisher excerpt independently shows external narration surrounding explicitly introduced journal material. The apparent first-person counterexamples are local: q02168 is Cope’s speech, and q02170 plus the journal sentence inside q02171 are embedded writings by Johnson. The brief faux-editorial introduction and occasional journal excerpts do not constitute sustained autonomous base sections, so they do not warrant ALTERNATING. No material uncertainty remains beyond the limited scope of the authorized excerpt.
